c.tagline: Highland capital of Tigray, gateway to Aksumite history and the otherworldly Danakil Depression.

taxi.fareNote: Shared minibus 'line taxis' run fixed routes for a small flat fare; private trips in blue-and-white taxis are not metered, so agree the fare before departure.

emergency.note: 911 is a general emergency line but is not always reliably staffed; hotel or tour operator assistance is often faster in practice.

avoid.reason: Avoid overland travel toward western Tigray and the Eritrean border areas, which remain volatile after the 2020–22 war.
Check security conditions before visiting; crime against visitors is low but fuel, cash and power shortages persist.

hood_desc: The commercial and administrative heart of Mekelle around the central square and Yohannes IV Palace Museum; best base for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.
A busy hotel and business district near the Tigray Martyrs' Memorial Monument, popular with conference travelers and NGO staff, with the city's liveliest restaurants and bars.
A largely residential district built around the well-known Ayder Referral Hospital; quiet and mostly local, with few tourist services.
A university district home to Mekelle University's Adi-Haki campus, with budget guesthouses and student-oriented cafes.
An outlying district near Alula Aba Nega International Airport, semi-rural and convenient for early flights but far from the center.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water; the municipal supply is unreliable.

transit.hours: Shared minibuses and Bajaj tuk-tuks run roughly 6:00 AM to 8:00-9:00 PM; little to no public transport after dark.
transit.pay: Cash paid directly to the driver or conductor; there is no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.note: There is no metro, tram, or formal city bus network; shared minibuses and blue three-wheeled Bajaj tuk-tuks are the main way to get around.

bus: Selam Bus and Sky Bus intercity coaches to Addis Ababa

tip.r: Not obligatory, but rounding up or leaving 5-10% at hotels and restaurants catering to travelers is appreciated.
